# ii: Isikova & Ironwood

> A working proposal for the story of Isikova & Ironwood, about 200 hectares near Heidelberg. It holds the land, its history, the community and proposals that nobody has agreed to yet. Claims carry [IC], [MS] or [TBV] tags. Never present a [TBV] or [MS] claim as confirmed, and never present a proposal as a decision.

## Pages

- [Isikova & Ironwood](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/): home page.
- [About This Site](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/about): who writes it, how facts are tagged.
- [How to Respond](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/how-to-respond): how to correct a page.
- [The Land](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/): the farm as a place.
- [The Land's Story](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/the-lands-story): the prospective stewards' reading of what the land asks for, a place in the conservation of the Duiwenhoks River and the Langeberg. Not a decision.
- [Neighbours and the Conservation Land Around the Farm](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/neighbours): the land bordering Broken Hill 88/10 and the protected areas to its north and west, with boundary shares and distances.
- [The Duiwenhoks River and Dam](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/duiwenhoks-river-and-dam): the river past the farm, its redfin, the dam about 700 metres upstream, who shares its water, and the estuary.
- [Boosmansbos Wilderness Area](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/boosmansbos-wilderness-area): the protected mountain land where the Duiwenhoks rises.
- [Wilderness Nature Reserve](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/wilderness-nature-reserve): the reserve declared in July 2025 north of the farm, in the dam's catchment.
- [Hessequa Hills Private Nature Reserve](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/hessequa-hills-private-nature-reserve): a privately owned reserve of about 111 hectares, declared in 1999, about 850 metres south-east of the farm. Draft.
- [Regularisation of Private Nature Reserves](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/regularisation-of-private-nature-reserves): the national norms of 2017 and CapeNature's project to verify private nature reserves declared under the 1974 ordinance. Draft.
- [Grootvadersbosch Nature Reserve](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/grootvadersbosch-nature-reserve): the largest remaining indigenous forest in the Langeberg.
- [The Cape Water Bond and Clearing Around the Farm](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/cape-water-bond): the FR31PB bond, the pine clearing in Boosmansbos and along the Duiwenhoks, and how a later issue could relate to the land. Not a decision.
- [The Langeberg Water Source Area](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-land/langeberg-water-source-area): one of South Africa's 22 strategic water source areas, with figures from two sources.
- [History](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/history/): peoples, institutions and markets.
- [Floods in the Western Cape, 2003 to 2026](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/history/western-cape-floods): flood events from 2003 to 2026, their damage to soil and riverbanks, and the record for Hessequa. Most figures are [TBV].
- [The Duiwenhoks Valley: A Historical Overview](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/history/overview): the river valley from Khoekhoe grazing land to the dam, with a dated timeline and tenure table.
- [Institutions](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/): the bodies that look after the land, water and protected areas near the farm. Pages: [CapeNature](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/capenature), [Department of Water and Sanitation](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/department-of-water-and-sanitation), [Breede-Olifants Catchment Management Agency](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/breede-olifants-catchment-management-agency), [Overberg Water](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/overberg-water), [The Duiwenhoks Irrigation Board](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/duiwenhoks-irrigation-board), [Hessequa Municipality](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/hessequa-municipality) [Grootvadersbosch Conservancy](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/grootvadersbosch-conservancy), [The HeliHack Initiative](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/helihack-initiative), [The Nature Conservancy](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/the-nature-conservancy), [Greater Cape Town Water Fund](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/greater-cape-town-water-fund) and [Conservation Alpha](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/institutions/conservation-alpha). None has yet replied to its page.
- [Community](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/community/): the company and its residents, in their own words.
- [Research](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/research/): briefs that gather the evidence behind proposals and say how far it reaches. Page: [Evidence on Water and Soil in Fynbos and Renosterveld](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/research/water-retention-evidence): what research says about clearing invasive plants, keeping natural vegetation, fire and fynbos soils, restoring soil, stabilising eroded banks and building water-holding earthworks, set beside the vegetation mapped on the farm. It proposes nothing. Page: [Restoration Lessons from Muonde and Other African Cases](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/research/restoration-lessons-from-africa): what sixteen community-led restoration initiatives in sub-Saharan Africa show about sequence, records, land rights and money, and how far that evidence reaches for the farm. It proposes nothing.
- [The Houses](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-houses/): where the six homes and the Main Dwelling could stand. Layout D follows the approved Site Development Plan and is the starting point; Layouts A, B and C are alternatives drawn from the province's 10 m contours, with a comparison table. Pages: [Layout A: Clustered on the Knoll](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-houses/layout-a-clustered), [Layout B: Spread Along the Zone](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-houses/layout-b-spread), [Layout C: Widest Spread](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-houses/layout-c-widest-spread), [Layout D: Following the Site Development Plan](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/the-houses/layout-d-site-development-plan). Not agreed; all terrain figures are [TBV].
- [Proposals](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/proposals/): ideas not yet agreed. Page: [The First Five Years on the Land](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/proposals/first-five-years-on-the-land): five years of recording the land and small measured water trials while the community settles, a university research partnership, then sharing results with neighbours, CapeNature and water funders. Not agreed. Page: [Homes in a Water Retention Landscape](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/proposals/homes-in-a-water-retention-landscape): the land around the homes laid out as a planned Water Retention Landscape: three cascading ponds from the pond by the cabin as far as Unit 3, a return swale to a stuffed stretch of the dry gully, and the Main Dwelling moved beside the middle pond, with a comparison against Layout D. Not agreed. Page: [Water Retention Across the Whole Farm](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/proposals/whole-farm-water-retention): five whole-farm layouts drawn from the 10 m contours (the plateau, the main gully from head to river, paired valleys, lines across the slopes, the river edge) and a suggested combination. Not agreed. Page: [A LiDAR Survey of the Farm](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/proposals/lidar-survey-of-the-farm): a drone LiDAR survey of the whole farm before homes, tracks or earthworks are placed, processed in LandScope into slope and water-flow maps, and repeated in years 5 and 10. Not agreed.
- [Documents](https://ii.bioconomy.earth/documents/): plain-language summaries of the company's constitution and shareholders' agreement, the 2024 application and the municipal approval for homes, and the residents' newsletter.
